## lore-reviewer App and the auto-merge loop lore-reviewer is a second GitHub App whose only job is to approve: GitHub refuses an approval from the App that opened a pull request, and Lore's own App opens the implementation loop's. The auto-merge loop approves as lore-reviewer when its three values are set (`LORE_REVIEWER_APP_ID`, `LORE_REVIEWER_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `LORE_REVIEWER_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`, mirrored into the stations service from Secret Manager behind `enable_lore_reviewer`), and as Lore's own App otherwise; a pull request Lore's App opened, with no lore-reviewer installed, is parked as "needs the lore-reviewer App" *(amended 2026-10-23: the approver setting and the two-key ceremony that guarded it are gone)*. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/lore/plans/ea73a044-33aa-44ab-8d08-19fe4e282156#p_0fb6ce5d-602d-4f29-99aa-3bc62a13b6f2)) The review line starts on PRs opened by Lore's own App. Today `decideReviewOnOpen` (`libs/shared/src/work/review/code-review-decisions.ts`) skips every PR whose author ends in `[bot]`, re-checks included, so no Lore-authored PR is ever reviewed on its own and lore-reviewer would never be asked to approve. Lore's App is let through; every other bot stays skipped. Lore's App is recognised by its own login, read once at startup with `GET /app` under the App's JWT (the App slug plus the `[bot]` suffix) and held in memory for the life of the process, so no login is hardcoded and every other bot still fails the plain `[bot]` suffix check. ([from plan](https://lore.gcp.re-cinq.com/repos/re-cinq/lore/plans/ea73a044-33aa-44ab-8d08-19fe4e282156#fe939733-53d6-4cde-a143-761995766fd3)) The loop's switch and its one setting live in `lore.repos.settings.auto_merge = { enabled, min_age_hours }` *(amended 2026-10-23)*: off by omission, and the minimum age a pull request must have been open before it merges, 24 hours when absent, negative or fractional. The switch is the **Auto merge** loop of the repo's Loops tab (`PUT /api/repos/{owner}/{repo}/loops/merge`, body `{ enabled }`, specs/implementation-loop FR7); switching it on asks nothing else. The minimum age is a field of the repo's Settings page, under Run policy, showing 24 until one is saved *(moved there 2026-10-23)*; a blank, negative or fractional value saves nothing. The settings save merges `auto_merge` key by key, so saving the hours keeps the switch as the Loops tab left it. Switching off takes back the auto-merge the loop armed, on Lore's own pull requests and on any the loop ran for; a disarm GitHub refuses, or a pull-request read that fails, is logged and never fails the switch. A repository with no row is a 404 before any GitHub read. The loop picks every open pull request code review has passed, whoever opened it: not a draft, on a branch of the repository itself (a fork's branch is one Lore cannot push a fix to), and with Lore's `lore/code-review` check approved on its head. The stations sweep `auto-merge-tick` (`cron.auto_merge.tick`, every 5 minutes) starts one `auto-merge` run per such pull request in every repository whose loop is on, skipping one a run is already working, at most 3 per repository per tick so a burst reaches the floor over a few ticks. Each run records the head commit it was started on (`head_sha`), and a pull request a run already worked on its current head, whether that run armed it or parked it, is taken again only once someone pushes to it. The `auto-merge` line (`libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/auto-merge.yaml`, one run per `pr_url`) waits at `await-merge`, a human station the `pr-ready-check` sweep answers, and fixes nothing *(amended 2026-10-23: the `auto-merge-fix` agent with its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations is gone; a loop pull request is rebased and repaired by the implementation loop on the pull request's own events, `specs/external-floor` FR12.19, and a person's pull request is the person's to fix)*. Each of these holds the wait, in order: a conflict or red CI; an open review thread, whether or not a review, re-check or reply run is still answering it; Lore's review not yet standing approved on the head, so after a push the run waits for the re-check, and a review that asked for changes; then the pull request waits out its minimum age; only then is it ready. A pull request GitHub did not say when it opened counts as old enough. No agent works for the auto-merge loop *(amended 2026-10-23)*: the line defines no agent definition, its wait produces nothing, and a pull request that is not ready is waited out until whoever owns it has put it right. # The auto-merge loop (specs/protected-branch-merge): one run per pull request code # review has passed. It waits until the pull request is green, every review thread # is resolved, Lore's review stands approved on its head and it has been open long # enough; then it approves and hands the merge to GitHub, or merges itself where no # rule asks for an approval. It fixes nothing on the way: a pull request that is # red, conflicted or behind is the business of the loop that opened it, which # rebases and repairs it on the pull request's own events; this loop only waits. line: id: auto-merge entry: await-merge exit: done args: repo: kind: git # One run per pull request: the loop starts it again only after a run ends. pr_url: kind: value subject: true # The head commit the run was started for: the loop takes a pull request # again only once its head moved past every run that worked it. head_sha: kind: value nodes: - id: await-merge station: auto-merge-await route: "{args.pr_url}" - id: approve station: auto-merge-approve - id: done edges: - from: await-merge to: approve on: success # The pull request was closed, or cannot be judged: nothing to merge. - from: await-merge to: done on: failed - from: approve to: done on: success - from: approve to: done on: failed stations: auto-merge-await: description: Waits on the pull request until CI is green, no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on its head and it has been open long enough. Red CI, a conflict or an open thread is waited out, never fixed here. kind: human outcomes: - success - failed needs: - name: head_sha kind: value produces: [] auto-merge-approve: description: Approves the pull request and arms GitHub's auto-merge where the branch rule asks for an approval, or merges it where it asks for none; a pull request touching a code owner's path, or one only Lore's own App could approve, is left for a person. kind: service outcomes: - success - failed needs: - name: pr_url kind: value produces: - name: merge_state kind: value - name: merge_blocked kind: value ## FR4 — Waiting on the pull request

While the loop is on, every open pull request Lore's review approved is taken up, whoever opened it. When its build is red or it conflicts with its base, an agent fixes it; when review threads are open, the agent answers each and resolves the ones its commit settled. Once CI is green, no thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head and the pull request has been open as long as the repository's Settings page asks (24 hours unless changed there), Lore approves it. Where the branch rule asks for an approval, GitHub's auto-merge is armed and GitHub merges; where it asks for none, Lore merges it. A pull request that changes a path a code owner must approve, or one the loop could not fix in three rounds, is left for a person under Parked. Lore approves the pull requests it opened itself as the lore-reviewer App, which has to be installed.

--- adr_number: 12 title: Autonomous Review Loop via LoreTask CRD status: draft date: 2026-04-01 domains: [agent, pipeline, review] --- # ADR-012: Autonomous Review Loop via LoreTask CRD Closes the review loop by automatically running an agent review after an implementation PR is opened, so it posts an APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict and iterates on the branch (up to two rounds) without waiting for a human. > **Mechanism update ([ADR-031](./ADR-031-agent-station-crds.md)).** The review-loop > decision stands, but it no longer runs on `LoreTask` CRs: the review is a `github_action` > + agent node in the Floor-side workflow graph (the `review` Agent posts the verdict; the > graph follows the `changes_requested` edge). The substrate is the ai-agent-subsystem. > **Widening: the `code-review` assembly line (2026-07 amendment).** The loop above > reviewed only Lore's **own** implementation PRs. The `code-review` assembly line > ([`code-review.yaml`](../libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/code-review.yaml)) widens > this to **any open PR on a repo with `auto_review` enabled** — driven by PR-lifecycle > webhooks on the event bus ([ADR-015](./ADR-015-webhook-driven-review-reactor.md)). It is > the **sole reviewer** (the legacy `review-reactor` was retired). The engagement is an > **event choreography** (wiring in [`floor-review-start.ts`](../libs/shared/src/work/review/floor-review-start.ts)): > > - **Triggers.** A **first, deep** review runs on `opened` / `reopened` / > `ready_for_review` / the first `synchronize` (`hasReviewedPr`). Every **later push** > starts the fast `code-review-recheck` line instead (2026-08 amendment below), so the > verdict tracks the fix; an explicit `@lore review` still forces a full re-review. The > first review posts a how-to "review started" comment; the re-check posts none. > - **Reviews submit a formal verdict** (2026-08 amendment). The `review` node emits > **structured findings** (`REVIEW_FINDINGS`) + a verdict; the Floor renders them as > **Conventional Comments** (with ` ```suggestion ` blocks) and posts ONE review whose > GitHub event **is** the verdict — `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`, no longer a neutral > `COMMENT`. It still never commits. > - **Comments are acted on only when asked.** A human comment starts a pass only when it > carries `@lore review` (*amended 2026-09-30*: the `comment-triage` Haiku classifier that > used to route every other comment was removed with the move to the external floor); a plain > comment starts nothing. > - **Fixes are human-gated.** A fix only happens when a human approves it via a reply. > - **State + merge gate.** Each PR-linked line publishes a `lore/` **check > run** (in_progress while running; `neutral` on changes-suggested); required in branch > protection it blocks merge only while the review runs. Lore's own auto-merge defers > with `review_in_flight` while a review line is open. > > Loop-prevention stays load-bearing: bot-authored PRs and bot comments (`…[bot]`) are > skipped so the review never re-triggers on its own output. The reused gate is > `shouldAutoReview()`. > **Formal verdict + two-phase review (2026-08 amendment).** Two coupled changes close the > merge loop: > > 1. **Formal `APPROVE` / `REQUEST_CHANGES`, always on.** The single posted review now > carries the verdict as its GitHub review event for **every** repo (not the > suggestion-only `COMMENT` of the original design), so it satisfies branch-protection > "require approvals" and the dark-factory `require_bot_approval` gate > ([ADR-016](./ADR-016-dark-factory-mode.md)). Derived in > [`post-review.ts`](../apps/stations/src/code-review/post-review/post-review.ts) from the > already-parsed `output.verdict`; the inline findings ride the same review. > 2. **A fast re-check on every push.** After the deep review, each new push starts the > cheap Haiku `code-review-recheck` line > ([`code-review-recheck.yaml`](../libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/code-review-recheck.yaml)), > which re-decides the verdict on the updated diff and re-submits it. Auto-merge reads > the bot's **latest** decision, so a later `REQUEST_CHANGES` overrides an earlier > `APPROVE` and vice-versa > . > > **Self-approval limit.** GitHub 422s when the review author is the PR author, so the bot > cannot `APPROVE` its **own** PR; that post degrades to a plain comment and auto-merge > stays deferred. Fully autonomous self-approval on Lore-authored PRs requires the reviewer > to run as a **distinct GitHub App identity** from the author (`LORE_REVIEW_BOT_LOGIN`) — > deployment config, not code.
**session-summary/2026-10-23-loop-pr-upkeep-auto-merge-no-fixer** (memory): PR re-cinq/lore#3376 (2026-10-23): the implementation loop keeps its pull requests mergeable on GitHub events; auto merge fixes nothing. DECISIONS (user): auto-merge must not fix anything — `auto-merge-fix`, `fix-pr`, `fix-replies` deleted, `decideMergeReady` answers ready|wait only; a loop PR is the loop's to rebase/repair, a person's PR is the person's. Rebase whenever a loop PR is behind main, not only when red. DESIGN: `await-pr` (decidePrReady) reads `mergeable` + `behindBy` (prBehindBy dep = repo.branchBehindBy, the same count loop-sync-check reads) BEFORE CI → `pr_conflicting`/`pr_behind` → changes_requested → sync-pr; sync edges iteration_max 6, fix stays 3. A settled loop PR that is behind/conflicted/red gets an UPKEEP RUN: the same implementation-loop line started with floor-client `lines.start(..., {entry: "sync-pr"})`, keyed on `backlog: upkeep-` so it never joins or holds `backlog:tickets`; start items task_id (taskQueue.latestLoopTaskByIssue) + ticket file (issue text) + pr_url. `apps/stations/src/events/loop-upkeep-handlers.ts` answers github.push (default branch only) and github.check_suite.completed; an open run on the branch → judgeFloorPullRequest (floor-ci-wait `only` filter) instead of a start. run-settled settles upkeep runs like any loop run (settlingTasks CAS no-ops on the completed task). BUG FIXED ON THE WAY: buildStationHandlers registered sweep events with Map.set, so two sweeps on one event overwrote each other (blocked-reason already declared both events); now addHandlers composes. LINT TRAPS: `events` layer may not import @re-cinq/floor-client (use LoopRunsFloor from shared); max-member-chain 2 hops; no-flag-params; max-lines-per-function 20; file max 300 (split pr-ready-check/sweep-reads.ts). `eslint --fix specs adrs` repoints anchors by test title but NOT short-label links like `[validated by pending waits]` — those need hand repointing. Shipped agent count test went 33→32. **session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: The auto-merge loop is designed to merge passed pull requests on protected branches. **session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: A settled loop pull request determines whether its build is red from the repository's own checks on the latest non-`[skip ci]` commit. **session:re-cinq/lore** (episode) [observed]: A pull request whose auto-merge run already settled on its current head commit stays armed or parked instead of starting a new run every 5 minutes until a new commit is pushed **session-summary/2026-09-12-repair-build-ci-verdict** (memory): Diagnosed assembly run 997026f5 (implementation-loop, issue #1510, PR #1684) and shipped PR #2039. FINDING: the run did not die running tests. Four rounds came back red on ONE job (format) for ONE eslint error (specs/testing-standards/spec.md:7 require-status-matches-coverage). await-ci returned `failed` (ci_red_unchanged) → repair-build. ciFeedbackOf (apps/floor/src/work/assembly-run/ci-feedback.ts) rendered the "CI reported failures" block only for incoming outcome changes_requested; the await-ci→repair-build edge fires on failed. So repair-build — the node the YAML says "is handed the failing checks" — got NO verdict, ran `npm ci` + `npm run build -w @re-cinq/lore-shared`, and died at the 1Gi pod limit (BackoffLimitExceeded) on a one-line fix. ci_failure_summary was "" because Actions check-run output is null; #2021 (09-11, after the run) added steps+tail; the annotations endpoint had the exact path:line message and nothing read it. SHIPPED (#2039, 4 commits): gate widened to failed+changes_requested; JobFailure.annotations (failure level, paginated) rendered first; explainFailedChecks moved from stations park-readers to shared check-runs.ts; new port reads listBranchCommits(repo, branch, limit) oldest-first + jobLog; lore-api GET /api/repos/:o/:r/ci-failures?branch|pr_number and /ci-jobs/:job_id/log?tail&grep; MCP tools lore_get_ci_failures / lore_get_ci_job_log in ci-tools.ts registered in registerSharedTools (agent gateway serves them), lore_get_pr_status moved beside them; detectCurrentBranch() in server-core repo-detect (uncached, null on detached HEAD). fix-ci prompt: act on annotation with an editor, ask CI via the tools, never reinstall/rebuild. NO migration: fix-ci org row is NULL since 0068 and resolves from the yaml in the image. OpenAPI + web-ui types + catalog seed regenerated; specs for both routes and both tools; FR15, shared-utilities, platform-infrastructure amended. DECISIONS: user first got my "keep reads Floor-side, no pod tools" recommendation, reaffirmed pod tools → treated as their call; then asked for branch-keyed inputs (a pod never reliably knows a PR number) → routes accept branch or pr_number, tool defaults branch from git. TRAPS: max-lines (300) hit on platform-github.ts (two-port adapter) → file-level eslint-disable with justification. Link re-anchoring needed a HEAD-line+title script handling empty labels, backticked labels, repo-root paths, untracked spec files, duplicate titles; run prettier BEFORE relink. memory-tools/pipeline-tools mcp tests fail locally pre-existing (clean HOME too) — judge by CI. **manual:28c28451-d416-4b50-af74-2e31b1a83870** (episode) [observed]: The auto-merge system had grown to include auto-merge-fix to cover PR watching.

--- adr_number: 12 title: Autonomous Review Loop via LoreTask CRD status: draft date: 2026-04-01 domains: [agent, pipeline, review] --- # ADR-012: Autonomous Review Loop via LoreTask CRD Closes the review loop by automatically running an agent review after an implementation PR is opened, so it posts an APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED verdict and iterates on the branch (up to two rounds) without waiting for a human. > **Mechanism update ([ADR-031](./ADR-031-agent-station-crds.md)).** The review-loop > decision stands, but it no longer runs on `LoreTask` CRs: the review is a `github_action` > + agent node in the Floor-side workflow graph (the `review` Agent posts the verdict; the > graph follows the `changes_requested` edge). The substrate is the ai-agent-subsystem. > **Widening: the `code-review` assembly line (2026-07 amendment).** The loop above > reviewed only Lore's **own** implementation PRs. The `code-review` assembly line > ([`code-review.yaml`](../libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/code-review.yaml)) widens > this to **any open PR on a repo with `auto_review` enabled** — driven by PR-lifecycle > webhooks on the event bus ([ADR-015](./ADR-015-webhook-driven-review-reactor.md)). It is > the **sole reviewer** (the legacy `review-reactor` was retired). The engagement is an > **event choreography** (wiring in [`floor-review-start.ts`](../libs/shared/src/work/review/floor-review-start.ts)): > > - **Triggers.** A **first, deep** review runs on `opened` / `reopened` / > `ready_for_review` / the first `synchronize` (`hasReviewedPr`). Every **later push** > starts the fast `code-review-recheck` line instead (2026-08 amendment below), so the > verdict tracks the fix; an explicit `@lore review` still forces a full re-review. The > first review posts a how-to "review started" comment; the re-check posts none. > - **Reviews submit a formal verdict** (2026-08 amendment). The `review` node emits > **structured findings** (`REVIEW_FINDINGS`) + a verdict; the Floor renders them as > **Conventional Comments** (with ` ```suggestion ` blocks) and posts ONE review whose > GitHub event **is** the verdict — `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`, no longer a neutral > `COMMENT`. It still never commits. > - **Comments are acted on only when asked.** A human comment starts a pass only when it > carries `@lore review` (*amended 2026-09-30*: the `comment-triage` Haiku classifier that > used to route every other comment was removed with the move to the external floor); a plain > comment starts nothing. > - **Fixes are human-gated.** A fix only happens when a human approves it via a reply. > - **State + merge gate.** Each PR-linked line publishes a `lore/` **check > run** (in_progress while running; `neutral` on changes-suggested); required in branch > protection it blocks merge only while the review runs. Lore's own auto-merge defers > with `review_in_flight` while a review line is open. > > Loop-prevention stays load-bearing: bot-authored PRs and bot comments (`…[bot]`) are > skipped so the review never re-triggers on its own output. The reused gate is > `shouldAutoReview()`. > **Formal verdict + two-phase review (2026-08 amendment).** Two coupled changes close the > merge loop: > > 1. **Formal `APPROVE` / `REQUEST_CHANGES`, always on.** The single posted review now > carries the verdict as its GitHub review event for **every** repo (not the > suggestion-only `COMMENT` of the original design), so it satisfies branch-protection > "require approvals" and the dark-factory `require_bot_approval` gate > ([ADR-016](./ADR-016-dark-factory-mode.md)). Derived in > [`post-review.ts`](../apps/stations/src/code-review/post-review/post-review.ts) from the > already-parsed `output.verdict`; the inline findings ride the same review. > 2. **A fast re-check on every push.** After the deep review, each new push starts the > cheap Haiku `code-review-recheck` line > ([`code-review-recheck.yaml`](../libs/assembly-lines/src/floor-pipelines/code-review-recheck.yaml)), > which re-decides the verdict on the updated diff and re-submits it. Auto-merge reads > the bot's **latest** decision, so a later `REQUEST_CHANGES` overrides an earlier > `APPROVE` and vice-versa > . > > **Self-approval limit.** GitHub 422s when the review author is the PR author, so the bot > cannot `APPROVE` its **own** PR; that post degrades to a plain comment and auto-merge > stays deferred. Fully autonomous self-approval on Lore-authored PRs requires the reviewer > to run as a **distinct GitHub App identity** from the author (`LORE_REVIEW_BOT_LOGIN`) — > deployment config, not code.

content.text: {"answer": "No. Lore's auto-merge loop does not fix a pull request whose CI is red. It only waits. As amended on 2026-10-23 (PR #3376), the `auto-merge` line has no agent. The `auto-merge-fix` agent and its `fix-pr` and `fix-replies` stations were deleted. The `await-merge` station is a human-kind wait, and `decideMergeReady` only answers ready or wait. Red CI gives the verdict `ci_red`. A conflict gives `pr_conflicting`. The loop holds the wait until whoever owns the pull request has fixed it. A pull request that the implementation loop opened is rebased and repaired by that loop on the pull request's own events (push and check_suite.completed), through 'upkeep' runs. A person's pull request is left for the person to fix. Once CI is green, no review thread is open, Lore's review stands approved on the head, and the minimum age has passed (24 hours by default), the loop approves and arms GitHub's auto-merge, or merges directly where no approval is required. One caveat: the web UI's `MergeExplainer.tsx` text still says an agent fixes red builds and parks pull requests after three failed rounds.
